Definition: Alemeth, the name of a place in Palestine and of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: The name belongs to two men and a town. Alemeth son of Becher is counted among the sons of Benjamin, and a later Alemeth is named in the line of Saul, son of Jehoadah; and the town of Alemeth in Benjamin was given to the priests with its suburbs; three uses, and the name is all the Bible says of any of them.
TheologicalSignificance: A name shared by two men and a town carries no lesson of its own. What it shows is how the Bible keeps the record straight, that even the men named only once in a list are counted, and the towns given to the priests are named.
